day_01_turn_of_the_monsoon.line: Shahbandar, land all 24 sacks of rice before the 10:15 tide.

port_day.line: Rice and pepper sail at 10:15, but the Kim Hong stays until 11:00.

rice.line: This trader carries the market’s 24 sacks of rice.

pepper.line: Pepper pays more duty than rice, but both ships leave at 10:15.

porcelain.line: The Kim Hong brings porcelain from Guangzhou and sails at 11:00.

resin.line: The Salamat brings frankincense from Cambay with a torn foresail.

tin.line: The Arus brings baskets of tin from Perak.

cloth.line: The Kaveri brings dyed cotton from Pulicat.

case_001.line: My ship carries porcelain and silk from Guangzhou, Shahbandar.

evidence.ev_manifest: Declared: 24 jars, 30 bowls each; 10 silk bales.
evidence.ev_testimony: Captain denies stopping after Champa; helmsman recalls two nights off Tioman.
evidence.ev_opened: Forward: 30 bowls; aft: 8 bowls over about 18 kati of nutmeg.

case_002.line: A porter says the Kaveri’s tally comes up one short.

evidence.ev_manifest: Declared: 2 kodi of cotton, one per bale.
evidence.ev_tally: Bale A: 20 rolls; bale B: 19, one with two loops.
evidence.ev_testimony: The captain counted 20 lengths per bale; the porter counted rolls.
evidence.ev_opened: Bale A yields 20 lengths; bale B’s thick roll yields two.

case_003.line: The quay weighers doubt the weight written on the Arus’s tin declaration.

evidence.ev_manifest: Seven baskets of tin, declared at 7 small bahar.
evidence.ev_exterior: The same tin reads 8 bahar on small scales, 7 on large.
evidence.ev_testimony: The boatman used the large scale and recorded 7 bahar.
evidence.ev_opened: Mud only outside; bare slabs still weigh 8 small bahar.

case_004.line: The Salamat’s captain won’t let porters behind the rear stack.

evidence.ev_manifest: 14 frankincense crates, 6 rosewater crates, no passengers; crate 11 resealed.
evidence.ev_exterior: Frankincense: 34–36 kati; crate 15: 94 kati; rosewater: 22–24 kati.
evidence.ev_testimony: The captain denies stopping in Sumatra; two crew recount Pedir.
evidence.ev_opened: Crate 3: two cracked flasks; crate 15: a man and letter.

ev_awang_musa_grievance.line: Awang Musa’s captain says more Perak boats will trade elsewhere if you hold them.

ev_bendahara_summons.line: Will the Gujarati ships stay when they hear of the warships off Pedir?

ev_kaveri_held_complaint.line: Sri Rangan’s agent asks who will pay for the Kaveri’s lost day.

ev_kaveri_keling_invitation.line: A messenger from Sri Rangan’s house invites you to dine with the Pulicat merchants.

ev_kim_hong_owner_plea.line: Tell the temenggung the porcelain and silk were honestly mine.

ev_kim_hong_whispers.line: Your clerk hears nutmeg is cheap in Upeh, but nobody says who brought it.

ev_lost_ship_agent.line: A broker offers to send your apology to a lost ship’s owners for a fee.

ev_rice_market_petition.line: The price of rice rose twice today; the sellers ask what you’ll do tomorrow.

ev_rice_market_thanks.line: The price of rice held, and a headman sends mangosteens in thanks.

ev_stranger_in_upeh.line: Your clerk heard that a wounded stranger from Pedir was seeking shelter in Upeh.

ev_two_dacing_petition.line: The head weigher asks you to make traders name the scale on tin declarations.
